title: Vehicle Communication Bus A (+) Open
plain: One of the two wires of vehicle communication network "A" (the + or "high" wire) seems to be broken or disconnected, so the car's computers can't talk to each other properly.
symptoms: Several warning lights on at once
Some gauges or features may stop working
Car may not start in some cases

causes.name: Broken network wire
Loose, unplugged or corroded connector
Pushed-out pin in a connector

checks: Test the battery and charging voltage
Check network resistance at the diagnostic port (about 60 ohms on most high speed CAN networks)
Unplug modules one at a time to find one pulling the network down
Inspect wiring in areas that see water, heat or movement
fix: Repair the broken wire or connector.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus A (+) Low
plain: The + ("high") wire of vehicle communication network "A" has lower voltage than it should, often because it's touching ground (bare metal) somewhere.
symptoms: Several warning lights on at once
Some gauges or features may stop working
Car may not start in some cases

causes.name: Network wire rubbed through and touching metal
Water or corrosion in a connector
A failed module shorting the network

checks: Test the battery and charging voltage
Check network resistance at the diagnostic port (about 60 ohms on most high speed CAN networks)
Unplug modules one at a time to find one pulling the network down
Inspect wiring in areas that see water, heat or movement
fix: Repair the shorted wire or connector, or replace the module that is shorting the network.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus A (+) High
plain: The + ("high") wire of vehicle communication network "A" has higher voltage than it should, often because it's touching a powered wire somewhere.

fix: Repair the shorted wire or connector, or replace the module that is shorting the network.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus E (-) shorted to Bus E (+)
plain: The two wires of vehicle communication network "E" seem to be touching each other, so messages between the car's computers get scrambled.
symptoms: Several warning lights on at once
Some gauges or features may stop working
Car may not start in some cases

causes.name: Network wires crushed or rubbed together
Water or corrosion bridging pins in a connector
A failed module shorting the network

checks: Test the battery and charging voltage
Check network resistance at the diagnostic port (about 60 ohms on most high speed CAN networks)
Unplug modules one at a time to find one pulling the network down
Inspect wiring in areas that see water, heat or movement
fix: Repair the shorted wires or connector, or replace the module that is shorting the network.

title: Software Incompatibility With Body Control Module "A"
plain: One of the car's computers found that the body control module "A" (which runs things like lights, locks and wipers) has software that doesn't match the rest of the car. This often shows up after a module was replaced or updated.
symptoms: Some lights, locks or other body features may act up
Other warning messages on some vehicles

causes.name: Module replaced or updated without the matching software
Programming that didn't finish
Wrong or used module installed

checks: Ask whether a module was recently replaced or updated
Check software levels in each module with a scan tool
Reprogram the module with the dealer's or a capable shop's tool
fix: Reprogram the body control module or the module that reported the code with the correct software.

title: Software Incompatibility With Multi-axis Acceleration Sensor Module "A"
plain: One of the car's computers found that the motion sensor module (it measures how the car is turning and tilting, mainly for stability control) has software that doesn't match. This often shows up after a module was replaced or updated.
symptoms: Stability control or traction control light on
ABS light on some vehicles

causes.name: Module replaced or updated without the matching software
Programming that didn't finish
Wrong or used module installed

checks: Ask whether a module was recently replaced or updated
Check software levels in each module with a scan tool
Reprogram and calibrate the sensor module with a capable scan tool
fix: Reprogram and calibrate the sensor module or the module that reported the code.
drive: Normal brakes and steering usually still work, but stability control may be off. Drive gently, leave extra room on wet or icy roads, and get it checked soon.

title: Invalid Data Received From Coolant Temperature Control Module
plain: Another computer in the car is getting signals from the coolant temperature control module that don't make sense, so engine or battery cooling may not be controlled correctly.
symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning light
Temperature warnings on some vehicles
Weak cabin heat on some vehicles

causes.name: Faulty coolant temperature control module or valve
Wiring or connector problem, including water in a connector
Software problem that an update may fix

checks: Check the module's connector for water or corrosion
Check coolant level with the engine cold
Ask the dealer about bulletins or software updates (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Usually a connector or wiring repair, a software update, or a new control module or valve.
drive: Watch the temperature gauge. If it climbs toward H, a red temperature light comes on or you see steam, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Never open a radiator or coolant cap while the engine is hot; it can spray scalding coolant. Otherwise get it checked in the next few days.
